title: Geometric Probability: Length and Area
standard_text: G.13B determine probabilities based on area to solve contextual problems
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.13B: geometric probability with lengths, areas, targets, spinners and circles inside squares. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Geometric probability = favorable length or area ÷ total length or area.
  • On a segment, use lengths. In a region, use areas.
  • For a spinner, use the angle of the sector ÷ 360°.
  • For circles, square the radii: a radius twice as big has 4 times the area.

Examples

Example

Bullseye radius 2, target radius 6

4π ÷ 36π

Answer: 1/9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the radius ratioArea uses r2.
Using the complementRead which region is asked for.
Dividing by the wrong totalDivide by the whole region.

faq.a: Determine probabilities based on area to solve contextual problems.

faq.q: What if the region is a sector?

faq.a: Yes, if the favorable region is the whole region.
Often it cancels; otherwise use 3.14 or a calculator.
